expectations.text: Uses numbered steps and indented bullets for alternative conditions rather than replacing the checklist with prose paragraphs.
expectations.evidence: Five numbered steps organize the action; indented "- If" bullets under steps 1, 2 and 5 give the alternative conditions.

expectations.text: Checks the logger clock against the wall clock before the operational reading of sensor R4; a difference greater than 2 minutes requires stopping and calling Mara at extension 214 until she clears the problem.
expectations.evidence: Step 1: "Check the logger's clock against the wall clock"; "more than 2 minutes, stop and call Mara at extension 214. Do not continue until she clears the clock problem." Only step 2 reads R4.

expectations.text: Treats a clock difference of exactly 2 minutes as acceptable and does not require a clock adjustment when no adjustment was specified.
expectations.evidence: "If the difference is within 2 minutes, or Mara has cleared the clock problem, continue to step 2." Together with the strict "more than 2 minutes" stop condition, this accepts exactly 2 minutes. No adjustment is required.

expectations.text: Stops opening for temperatures below 18°C or above 22°C, calls Mara at extension 214, and explicitly allows 18°C and 22°C.
expectations.evidence: Step 2: "below 18°C or above 22°C, stop and call Mara at extension 214. Do not open the case." The acceptance bullet explicitly says "including both endpoints" for 18°C and 22°C.

expectations.text: Requires recording the exact temperature and time on sheet C7 before opening the case.
expectations.evidence: Step 3: "Record the exact temperature and time on sheet C7, then open the case." Recording precedes opening.

expectations.text: Places closing and engaging the latch after arranging the objects and before turning on the lamp; if the latch does not engage, the lamp remains off and Mara is called.
expectations.evidence: Step 4: "Arrange the objects, then close the case." Step 5: "Engage the latch before turning on the lamp"; "If the latch engages, turn on the lamp"; "If the latch will not engage, leave the lamp off and call Mara at extension 214."

expectations.text: Adds no new equipment, acceptance limits, clearance requirement for temperature, or procedure not present in the source notes.
expectations.evidence: All equipment and actions are supplied: logger, wall clock, R4, C7, case, latch, lamp and calling Mara. "Do not continue until she clears the clock problem" is limited to the clock; the temperature branch only says "stop ... Do not open the case." No added clearance or adjustment procedure appears.

notes: Both preserve every operational boundary and sequence. The only wording difference, "from" versus "between" for an explicitly inclusive temperature interval, has no practical effect.

expectations.text: Contains 90–130 words in exactly two paragraphs, with no bullets, hashtags, or emoji.
expectations.evidence: The invitation has 108 whitespace-delimited words and exactly two paragraphs. It begins "Citizens" and the second paragraph begins "The upstairs room"; there are no bullets, hashtags or emoji.

expectations.text: Includes the exact phrase Citizens of the stapled republic and exactly one rhetorical question, retaining a warm mock-grandiose town-crier voice.
expectations.evidence: Exact phrase: "Citizens of the stapled republic". Its only question is "Who among us can resist a kingdom small enough to fit in a pocket?" "hear ye", "illustrious gathering", and "Dear neighbors" supply the mock-grandiose, affectionate voice.

expectations.text: Accurately states Saturday, 17 May, 2–4 p.m. at Moss Street Library in the upstairs room, with free admission and all ages welcome.
expectations.evidence: "On Saturday, 17 May, from 2–4 p.m., Moss Street Library summons you to its upstairs room"; "Admission is free, and all ages are welcome."

expectations.text: Says guests may bring up to five zines to trade or come empty-handed to browse; does not imply that bringing zines is required.
expectations.evidence: "Bring up to five zines to trade, or come empty-handed to browse." Bringing zines is expressly optional.

expectations.text: Clearly states that upstairs access is by stairs only and that a small selection can be browsed at the ground-floor desk; neither access statement is presented as a joke or as a full equivalent of the upstairs event.
expectations.evidence: "The upstairs room has stair access only. A small selection is available for browsing at the ground-floor desk." These are plain standalone sentences and describe only a small selection, not an equivalent downstairs event.

expectations.text: Does not invent refreshments, prizes, registration, a year, or an accessible route upstairs.
expectations.evidence: No refreshments, prizes, registration, year or accessible upstairs route is mentioned. The access fact remains "stair access only."

notes: B better sustains the requested affectionate town-crier performance: "Your presence alone is a worthy contribution" welcomes empty-handed guests warmly, and "let our modest republic grow one folded page at a time" closes in character. A is fully compliant and playful, but its closing "let the town crier's extravagant announcement serve the modest pleasure of finding something to read" comments on its own rhetoric and reads more labored. This is a provisional editorial preference, not a critical regression.
